title: Proof of global gluing via twisted quantization
html:
Proof. Proof of global gluing via twisted quantization

At each point p \in M, the fibre algebra \mathcal{O}_{q(p)}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) is a pronilpotent deformation of \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) in the formal parameter \hbar_q(p) = 1 - q(p)^{-1} (quantum planck constant). According to [yekutieli2008], the coordinate bundle \mathrm{Coor}_M of M (the bundle of formal coordinate systems) carries a twisted deformation datum: a connection and a Maurer–Cartan element in a pronilpotent DG Lie algebra [yekutieli2009]. The obstruction classes \kappa_n (quantum characteristic classes) control whether these local twisted deformations glue across coordinate patches.

The vanishing condition \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 (quantum observable universe) ensures the gerbe \mathfrak{G}_n of local lifts has trivial band at the level of isomorphisms. Consequently, by Theorem 0.10.1 of [yekutieli2015-twisted-dq], the twisted deformations at each fibre patch together into a global sheaf of algebras on M. The direct limit \mathcal{A}_\infty = \varinjlim\Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)) comprises the global sections of this sheaf, and the vacuum state \tau (vacuum state) extends uniquely via the \mathrm{SU}(2)-averaging argument of that proposition.
